questions.text: A certain sum of money amounts to Rs. 720 in 2 years and Rs. 870 in 4.5 years, with same rate of simple interest. Find the sum.
questions.explanation:
Given:

Amount in 2 years = Rs. 720

Amount in 4.5 years = Rs. 870

 Formula used:

Simple interest(SI) = [Principal(P) × Rate × Time] / 100

And Amount = Principal + SI

Calculation:

Let the sum(principal) be P and the rate of interest be R

So, 720 = Principal + SI

⇒ 720 = P + (P × R × 2)100      ......(i)

And 870 = P + SI

⇒ 870 = P + (P × R × 4.5)/100        ......(ii)

Equation (ii) - (i)

(2.5 × P × R)/100 = 150

⇒ P × R = 6000         ......(iii)

Now, from eq.(i),

720 = P + (6000 × 2)/100

⇒ P = 720 - 120 = Rs. 600

∴ The sum is Rs. 600

questions.text: A and B borrowed Rs.  15,000 and Rs. 18,000 respectively at the same rate of interest for 3 (1/2) years. If B paid Rs. 315 more interest than A. Find the rate of interest.
questions.explanation:
Given:

Simple interest paid by  B – Simple interest paid by A = Rs. 315

Principal for B = Rs. 18,000; Principal for A = Rs. 15,000

Formula used:

S.I. = ( P × R × T)/100

Where P, R and T represents Principal, rate and time respectively.

Calculation:

(18,000 × r × 3.5/100) – (15,000 × r × 3.5/100) = 315

⇒630r - 525 r = 315

⇒105 r = 315

⇒r = 3 %

∴ Rate is 3% per annum.

questions.text: Rs. 5,500 is invested in three parts all at simple interest of 5% p.a. These three parts are invested for 2 years, 4 years and 6 years respectively such that the interest received from the given three parts after desired period of investment is same. Find the difference between the smallest and the largest part of the investment.

The rate of interest on a sum of money is 4% per annum for the first 2 years, 6% per annum for the next 4 years and 8% per annum for the period beyond 6 years. If the simple interest accrued on the sum for a total period of 9 years is Rs. 1680, what is the sum?
questions.explanation:
Let,

Sum invested  = P

Simple Interest = (P x R x T) / 100

Therefore,

SI at the rate of 4% for 2 years = ( P × 4 × 2) / 100 = 2P / 25

SI at the rate of 6% for 4 years = ( P × 6 × 4 ) / 100 = 6P / 25

Therefore,

Remaining time = 9 - ( 2 + 4) = 3 years

Thus,

SI for the next 3 years = ( P × 8 × 3 ) / 100 = 6P / 25

Total SI incurred over period of 9 years = (2P / 25) + (6P / 25) + (6P / 25) = 14P / 25

Total SI after 9 years is 1680

Therefore,

14P / 25 = 1680

P = (1680 x 25) / 14

P = Rs. 3000

questions.text: A sum is invested at the rate of 5% per annum on simple interest, amounts Rs. 132 in 2 years. The same sum is invested at twice the previous rate at simple interest per annum for 3.5 years amounts-
questions.explanation:
Solution:

Formula Used:

SI = Amount – Principal

SI = P × T × R /100

Calculations:

Let the principal be Rs. x.

Amount = Rs. 132

SI = 132 – x      ----(1)

Also SI = x × 2 × 5 /100      ----(2)

Equating equation (1) and (2)

⇒ x × 2 × 5 /100 = 132 – x

⇒ 11x = 1320

⇒ x = 120

If the rate becomes two times i.e. 10% per annum,

⇒ SI = 120 × 3.5 × 10 /100

⇒ SI = 42

⇒ Amount = 120 + 42 = Rs. 162

Hence it amounts Rs. 162 at the rate 10% for 3.5 years.

questions.text: Three persons P, Q and R lend Rs. 4000, Rs. x and Rs. 5000 respectively at 6% rate of interest for 5 years. If the interest received after 5 years from Q and R is Rs. 2850. Then find the difference between the interest received by the P and Q.
questions.explanation:
Given:

Amount lent by P = ₹4000

Amount lent by Q = ₹x

Amount lent by R = ₹5000

Rate of interest (r) = 6%

Time (t) = 5 years

Interest from Q and R = ₹2850

Formula used:

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × r × t) / 100

Calculation:

Interest from R: SIR = (5000 × 6 × 5) / 100

⇒ SIR = ₹1500

Interest from Q: SIQ = ₹2850 - ₹1500

⇒ SIQ = ₹1350

(x × 6 × 5) / 100 = 1350

⇒ (30x) / 100 = 1350

⇒ 30x = 1350 × 100

⇒ x = 135000 / 30

⇒ x = ₹4500

Interest received by P: SIP = (4000 × 6 × 5) / 100

⇒ SIP = ₹1200

Interest received by Q: SIQ = ₹1350

Difference between SIP and SIQ = ₹1350 - ₹1200

⇒ Difference = ₹150

∴ The difference between the interest received by P and Q is ₹150.

questions.text: The amount of a certain sum with simple interest for 15 years is Rs. 439.80 and with simple interest for 7.5 years more is 523.047. Find the rate percent per annum (approx.) at which interest is reckoned?
questions.explanation:
Shortcut Trick

Interest for 7.5 years = Amount(22.5 yrs) − Amount(15 yrs) = ₹523.047 − ₹439.80 = ₹83.247

Interest for 15 years = 2 × ₹83.247 = ₹166.494

Principal (P) = ₹439.80 − ₹166.494 = ₹273.306

Rate (R) = (SI15 × 100) ÷ (P × T) = (166.494 × 100) ÷ (273.306 × 15) ≈ 4%

∴ The correct answer is 4%.

Alternate Method

Given:

Amount after 15 years (A1) = ₹439.80

Amount after 22.5 years (A2) = ₹523.047

Formula Used:

SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

Amount = P + SI

Calculations:

⇒ SI for 7.5 years = A2 − A1 = 523.047 − 439.80 = ₹83.247

⇒ SI for 1 year = 83.247 ÷ 7.5 = ₹11.0996

⇒ SI for 15 years = 11.0996 × 15 = ₹166.494

⇒ Principal (P) = A1 − SI15 = 439.80 − 166.494 = ₹273.306

⇒ Rate (R) = (SI for 1 year × 100) ÷ P

⇒ R = (11.0996 × 100) ÷ 273.306

⇒ R = 1109.96 ÷ 273.306 ≈ 4.06%

∴ The correct answer is 4%.

Additional Information

Simple Interest Nature

In Simple Interest, the interest remains constant every year as it is always calculated on the original Principal.

Rate Calculation

Rate % = (SI for 1 year ÷ Principal) × 100. Always ensure the Principal and Interest are for the same sum.

Difference between SI and CI

For the first year (if compounded annually), Simple Interest and Compound Interest are equal on the same principal and rate.

questions.text: If the annual rate of simple interest increases from 10% to \(12 \frac{1}{2}\%\), a man’s yearly income increases by Rs. 1,250. His principal (in Rs.) is

options.text: More than one of the above

questions.explanation:
Given:

Initial interest rate = 10%

Final interest rate = 12.5%

Increase in income = Rs. 1,250

Formula Used:

The increase in income is caused by the difference in interest earned at the two rates. We can use the formula for simple interest:

Interest = Principal x Rate x Time

Since the time (one year) remains constant, we can express the difference in interest as:

Increase in income = Difference in interest = P x (Final rate - Initial rate)

Calculation:

Let Principal be P

\(1250 = {P \over100} \times (12.5 - 10)\)

\(1250 \times 100= {P} \times (2.5)\)

\({P} ={{1250 \times 100}\over2.5}\)

P = 50,000

Therefore, the man's principal is Rs. 50,000.

questions.text: A man lends a certain sum of money at simple interest. Rate of interest for first one and a half years is 8%, for next 6 months is 10%, for next 10 months is 12% after that 4%. If he received Rs. 11200 as interest at the end of 4 years and 1 months, Find the principal.
questions.explanation:
Let the principal be Rs. P.

Now,

The simple interest for first one and a half year = (P × 8 × 3/2)/100

⇒ 12P/100

The Simple interest for next 6 months = (P × 10 × 1/2)/100

⇒ 5P/100

The Simple interest for next 10 months = (P × 12 × 10/12)/100

⇒ 10P/100

The Simple interest for the remaining 15 months = (P × 4 × 15/12)/100

⇒ 5P/100

According to question,

12P/100 + 5P/100 + 10P/100 + 5P/100 = 11200

⇒ 32P/100 = 11200

⇒ P = 11200 × 100/32

∴ P = Rs. 35000

questions.text: Neeraj invests an amount of Rs. 12,000 for three years. The rate of interest for the first, second, and, third-year respectively are 10%, 5%, and 15%. Find the interest earned after three years.
questions.explanation:
Given:

The amount invested = Rs. 12,000

Interest earned for first-year = 10%

Interest earned for second year = 5%

Interest earned for the third year = 15%

Concept used:

Simple interest = PNR/100

P – Principal

N – number of terms

R – Rate of interest

SI for three years = SI for 1st year + SI for 2nd year + SI for 3rd year

Calculation:

SI for 1st year = 12,000 × 1 × 10/100

⇒ SI for 1st year = Rs. 1,200

SI for 2nd year = 12,000 × 1 × 5/100

⇒ SI for 2nd year = Rs. 600

SI for 3rd year = 12,000 × 1 × 15/100

⇒ SI for 3rd year = Rs. 1,800

SI for three years = Rs. 1,200 + Rs. 600 + Rs. 1,800

⇒ SI for three years = Rs. 3,600

Rate of interest for three years together= Rate of interest for (1st-year +2nd year + 3rd year)

Rate of interest for three years together = 30%

Rate of interest for one year at 30% rate = Rate of interest for (1st-year +2nd year + 3rd year)

Interest after three years = 12,000 × 1 × 30/100

⇒ Interest after three years = Rs. 3,600.

∴ The interest earned after three years is Rs.3,600.
